analysis.investment_thesis: Anupam Rasayan fails the Magic Formula on both dimensions simultaneously — earnings yield of ~2.5% (EBIT INR 401 Cr / EV ~INR 15,951 Cr) and ROCE of just 7.3% — while revenue is contracting from its 2023 peak and free cash flow has been deeply negative for four of the last five years. A P/E of 85x on shrinking earnings is the worst valuation-to-return combination in this set.
key_strengths: Custom synthesis and manufacturing model creates long-term supply agreements with global agrochemical and pharma majors — some degree of contract visibility
Operating margin of 18.2% and gross margin of 44% are reasonable for a specialty chemicals compounder
Heavy capex cycle (CWIP hit INR 609 Cr in 2024 before falling to 58 Cr in 2025) may set up future capacity utilisation gains if demand recovers
key_risks: Revenue declined from INR 1,602 Cr (2023) to INR 1,437 Cr (2025) — the agrochemical downcycle is compressing the top line just as interest costs doubled to INR 112 Cr
FCF was -INR 440 Cr in FY2025 and cumulatively negative by over INR 1,200 Cr in the last 4 years — the capex cycle has consumed far more cash than it has generated
ROCE of 7.3% and ROE of 3.3% are deeply sub-par; the business is currently destroying rather than creating value on incremental capital deployed
red_flags: ROCE of 7.3% is less than half the 15% cost of equity — capital allocation has been value-destructive at current return rates
P/E of 85x on INR 160 Cr net profit with a declining revenue trajectory is extremely speculative pricing with no earnings support
Earnings yield of ~2.5% is near the bottom of any screen I run — both the quality AND the cheapness tests fail completely
analysis.detailed_analysis: This is the clearest avoid in the group. The Magic Formula requires a company to rank highly on both earnings yield (cheapness) and return on capital (quality); Anupam Rasayan fails both emphatically. EBIT of INR 401 Cr against an enterprise value of ~INR 15,951 Cr implies an earnings yield of just 2.5%, when I require at least 12–15%. Simultaneously, ROCE of 7.3% and ROE of 3.3% indicate the balance sheet is not earning its cost of capital. Heavy capex spending (INR 716 Cr in FY2024, INR 410 Cr in FY2025) funded by rising debt (borrowings up to INR 1,223 Cr) is compounding the problem — the company is deploying capital at well below acceptable returns while the agrochemical sector works through an inventory destocking cycle.
